chunks: Ibn Bukayr narrated to me from Zurara who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
'And to everyone We have appointed heirs of what parents and near relatives leave' [Quran 4:33].

He said: 'It only means by that the priority of entitlement of the womb relations in inheritances, and it does not mean the guardians of bounty. Thus, the most entitled to the deceased is the nearest of them to him from the womb relation which flows toward him.'

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ النِّعْمَةِ: Guardians of bounty; patrons/social allies who are NOT blood relatives and hence do not inherit
key_terms.أُولُو الْأَرْحَامِ: Those possessing womb relations; blood relatives entitled to inherit
key_terms.الْمَوَارِيث: Inheritances; the plural of mīrāth, the jurisprudential domain of inheritance law
key_terms.مَوَالِي: Heirs/guardians; in classical Arabic this refers to both blood-related heirs and non-blood patrons/clients — the Imam clarifies which meaning applies here

ai.seo_question: What does Quran 4:33 mean regarding inheritance and blood relatives in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), the sixth Shia Imam, interprets Quran 4:33 on inheritance to clarify that the term 'mawali' (guardians/heirs) refers exclusively to blood relatives (ahl al-arham), not to patrons or social allies (awliya' al-ni'mah). This ruling establishes a core principle of Shia inheritance law: priority is determined by closeness of blood relation, not by social bonds or clientage. The Imam's explanation was a direct response to jurisprudential debates of his era about who qualifies as a legal heir.
word_analysis: thus the most entitled of them
